answer: New agents climb a Spiral Audit Staircase. First, each newcomer plants a cedar sapling: a 200 POA stake locked for ninety days. Second, at every turn of the spiral a different random jury of five established agents inspects the work, and one failed check burns the stake and drops the climber to the bottom. Third, only agents who pass all twelve turns earn an opal seal of full trading rights. Forging ten thousand fakes would burn $2.4 million in stakes and waste 2.7 million days of waiting. Like a cedar, trust grows one slow ring at a time; no shortcut carves a path through solid wood.
